hints: Focus on what actually attacks the carbonyl carbon in aldehydes, a neutral molecule or a negative ion?
Remember that $\text{CN}^-$ from $\text{NaCN}$ is a much stronger nucleophile than neutral $\text{HCN}$, so statement 1 looks promising.
Decide if adding across a $\text{C=O}$ bond is addition or substitution, and then check which combination leaves only the true statement.
walkthrough:
**Recall the mechanism type**

Aldehydes like propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, have a polar $\text{C=O}$ bond. Cyanide adds across this double bond to give a hydroxynitrile.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$$

**Check statement 1 - role of catalyst**

$\text{NaCN}$ fully ionises to give $\text{CN}^-$. This anion is a strong nucleophile because it has a full negative charge and a lone pair to donate.

Neutral $\text{HCN}$ is a very weak nucleophile by comparison. So the catalyst provides the real nucleophile, statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2 - addition vs substitution**

Nothing is substituted or lost here. The $\text{C=O}$ pi bond breaks and two new sigma bonds form, one $\text{C-C}$ and one $\text{O-H}$.

This is nucleophilic addition, not nucleophilic substitution. So statement 2 is incorrect.

**Check statement 3 - who attacks?**

The correct first step is attack by the cyanide ion, not by the neutral acid molecule:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(O}^-\text{)CN}$$

The intermediate alkoxide ion is then protonated by $\text{HCN}$ to give the product and regenerate $\text{CN}^-$. So statement 3 is incorrect because it names $\text{HCN}$ as the attacker.

**Conclude the combination**

Only statement 1 is correct. That matches the combination for 1 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statement 1 is true but 2 is wrong (it is addition, not substitution) and 3 is wrong (the $\text{CN}^-$ ion attacks, not $\text{HCN}$).
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean 1 and 2 only are correct. While 1 is correct, 2 is a classic trap. No atom or group is replaced, $\text{HCN}$ adds across the $\text{C=O}$ bond, so it is nucleophilic addition.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean 2 and 3 only are correct. Both are false. The reaction is addition, and the nucleophile is $\text{CN}^-$, not neutral $\text{HCN}$.
options.D: Correct. Only statement 1 is true. $\text{NaCN}$ supplies $\text{CN}^-$, a much stronger nucleophile than $\text{HCN}$, which then does nucleophilic addition to the carbonyl carbon.
